milestone.title: M3 — Networks, a city tap, and a server that makes heat
milestone.description: Systems compose. Exit gate: on the starter world, tap the city feeder, wire a server, watch it draw power and warm the rock around it on the thermal overlay; tap the water main and fill a reservoir through pipe packets; all headless in CI with networks under 0.3 ms, buildings under 0.5 ms, the whole tick under 4.5 ms, deterministic and allocation-free. Also closes the two bugs found in review: water that loses its identity when it flows, and dug cells that need a suit. 22 tasks, 30.5 dev-days estimated, ~40 with contingency.

tasks.title: M3-23 Liquid pass measured in a player build, not the editor
tasks.body:
**Why this is needed.** M3-19 measured the liquid pass at 4.79 ms in Unity edit mode and found that
only 1.57 ms of it is the Burst kernel. The other 3.2 ms is `LiquidSystem`'s own managed work,
which the editor runs under Mono rather than IL2CPP. That number is an upper bound, not a cost,
and every decision about what to optimise next rests on knowing the real one.

**What it achieves.** One representative figure for the liquid pass on the breach scenario, taken from a
player build with the same split between kernel and managed remainder that the edit-mode test
reports, so the two can be compared directly.

- [ ] A headless player build that runs the breach scenario for a fixed tick count and reports the same fields as the edit-mode test
- [ ] Kernel and managed-remainder split reported separately, as in M3-19
- [ ] The figure recorded in ARCHITECTURE.md next to the edit-mode and headless ones, with the build configuration named
- [ ] Whether the 1.2 ms budget is reachable without further work, answered from that figure

Done when: The liquid pass has a number from a player build and ARCHITECTURE.md says what it was measured on.

tasks.title: M3-24 Bound LiquidSystem's per-tick grid work by the awake spans
tasks.body:
**Why this is needed.** `LiquidSystem.Tick` copies mass, element, flags and contamination across the whole
grid every tick, then scans the whole grid again to diff identity. That is roughly 1.5 MB of
copying and a full-grid pass in a system whose entire design is that cost follows activity.
M3-19 measured the managed remainder at 3.2 ms against a 1.2 ms budget for the whole pass, so
this is the larger of the two remaining costs.

**What it achieves.** The bookkeeping around the solve scales with what is awake, the same way the solve
itself already does, without changing what any of it computes.

- [ ] The four `CopyTo` calls bounded by the awake spans the solver already derives
- [ ] `MarkIdentityChanges` bounded the same way
- [ ] Grid hashes bit-identical to the current behaviour across the breach scenario, by the M3-19 comparison
- [ ] The managed remainder re-measured and recorded

Done when: The liquid pass costs what activity costs, and the breach scenario hashes exactly as it did before.

tasks.title: M3-25 Fewer, fatter liquid jobs
tasks.body:
**Why this is needed.** One `BurstLiquidKernel.Step` schedules 23 parallel-for jobs — two setup stages,
five per substep across four substeps, and the finish — each splitting 384 rows into 48
batches. The kernel measures 1.57 ms against a 1.2 ms line, and at this grid size the dispatch
may cost more than the arithmetic it dispatches. Nothing else about the kernel is known to be
slow.

**What it achieves.** The kernel inside its budget, or evidence that dispatch was not where the time went.

- [ ] Dispatch cost measured against arithmetic before anything is changed, so the premise is tested first
- [ ] Stages merged or batch size raised where the measurement says it pays
- [ ] Bit-identical grids to the C# reference on every M3-19 test, unchanged
- [ ] Target: kernel `Step` inside 1.2 ms on the breach scenario

Done when: The kernel is inside 1.2 ms, or the measurement says dispatch was not the cost and records what is.
